::: {#sol-cutoff-criterion}

It kept the cutoff that got the fewest images wrong.
Counting mistakes uses the 0-1 [loss function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-loss-function):
1 for a wrong label and 0 for a right one.
Its average over the images is the rule's [error rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-error-rate),
which is the rule's [empirical risk](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-empirical-risk) under that loss.
Choosing the [parameter](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-parameter) with the lowest empirical risk is [empirical risk minimization](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-empirical-risk-minimization),
and deep networks are fit the same way.

:::
